page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates support for modern instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and AES cryptographic acceleration. Memory is provisioned with 128 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external block storage for persistent or scratch space, and the system does not include discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and memory performance. The AMD EPYC architecture delivers top-quartile results across CPU benchmarks, registering 3,077.07 in single-core and 98,309.6 in multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 18,345.0. PassMark results align with this profile, highlighted by strong scores in overall CPU performance, extended instruction sets, encryption, and database operations. Memory subsystem tests show strong cached bandwidth of 4,398.68 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 102.49 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput in-memory data processing, evidenced by 67.43 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Instruction set extensions enable fast execution for lightweight machine learning tasks, placing small model prompt processing in the top ten percent of tested servers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.8xlarge offers solid resource density by providing dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead, ensuring predictable execution times under sustained concurrent utilization. The primary tradeoff centers on the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and absence of hardware acceleration, which shifts storage costs to networked block devices and bounds machine learning capabilities to CPU execution. The platform is well matched for mid-to-large relational databases, distributed caching layers, software compilation clusters, backend application serving, and enterprise ETL data pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system incorporates 128 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 core-to-memory configuration alongside 12 Gbps of baseline networking. It contains no onboard local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reflect upper-quartile execution speeds across single-core and multi-core evaluations, including strong results in PassMark database operations, cryptographic processing, and Redis throughput at 67.43 million operations per second. Hardware support for AVX-512 extensions further enhances performance for integer manipulation, encryption, and lightweight language model inference. The instance delivers consistent processing density without hyperthreading contention, making it appropriate for relational database management systems, in-memory caching fleets, continuous integration compilation jobs, and high-throughput application servers.
